html:
The Yakama are a Native American people of the Yakima River valley and the Columbia Plateau in eastern Washington state. They speak Sahaptin. Today about 10,000 are enrolled in the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation.

They fished for salmon at the great falls of the Columbia, such as Celilo Falls, gathered roots and berries, and hunted. After horses reached the plateau in the 1700s, they also travelled east to hunt bison. Their neighbours included the Palouse, the Wanapum and the Nez Perce.

In 1855 Yakama leaders signed a treaty at Walla Walla that gave up much of their land but kept a reservation and fishing rights. Gold miners soon crossed the reservation, and the Yakima War followed from 1855 to 1858. Their fishing rights, won in that treaty, were upheld by US courts in the 1900s. See also Yakima.
